document_check.note: Wang J, Zhang W, Zhou Y, Jia J, Li Y, Liu K, Ye Z, Jin L (2022) 'Altered Prefrontal Blood Flow Related With Mild Cognitive Impairment in Parkinson's Disease: A Longitudinal Study', Front. Aging Neurosci. 14:896191. It is a 2-year longitudinal ASL-MRI study of 49 cognitively normal PD patients (10 converters to MCI) and 37 healthy controls. The cited left lateral orbitofrontal CBF finding is reported on page 5.

cited_result: Converters to PD-MCI showed a greater 2-year decline in left lateral orbitofrontal CBF than non-converters: 25.8% versus 7.8%, subgroup x visit interaction p = 0.036. The authors read this as independent of cortical atrophy.
tool_reason: The cited result is the association of one factor (longitudinal prefrontal CBF decline) with a later clinical outcome (conversion to MCI at 2 years) in a cohort, not a multivariable model and not an exposure effect framed causally, so QUIPS fits best. The factor is measured over the same interval as the outcome, and this is noted below.

domains.rationale: The paper names the clinic source, recruitment period and eligibility criteria and describes the baseline sample. It does not say whether sampling was consecutive, how many patients were eligible or what the participation rate was. Six patients were excluded after recruitment for imaging reasons, and their characteristics are not reported.

signalling.question: Is the source population and the method of recruitment (consecutive or other) adequately described, with participation of eligible persons reported?
signalling.quote: In total 49 patients with PD were recruited from the movement disorders clinically at the Zhongshan Hospital from September 2016 to October 2018.

signalling.question: Are inclusion and exclusion criteria adequately described?
signalling.quote: (3) Hoehn and Yahr stages 1–2; (4) age 40–80 years; and (5) education >6 years. Exclusion criteria included the following: (1) a history of other neurologic or psychiatric diseases; (2) alcohol or drug abuse; or (3) contraindication to MRI.

signalling.question: Is the baseline study sample adequately described for key characteristics?
signalling.quote: TABLE 2 | Demographic, clinical, and neuropsychological data of converters and non-converters (means, SDs, and statistic differences).

signalling.question: Are post-recruitment exclusions described, with characteristics of those excluded?
signalling.quote: Six additional patients were excluded from data analysis because of excessive head motion during scanning (n = 1), MRI artifacts (n = 3), or poor MRI co-registration (n = 2).

domains.rationale: All 49 analysed patients have a 2-year classification, and the paper reports no loss to follow-up. The six exclusions were for stated technical reasons. The paper does not say at which visit these exclusions occurred.

signalling.question: Is the proportion of the baseline sample available for analysis adequate?
signalling.quote: After 2 years (V1), 10 patients with PD converted to MCI (converters), and 39 patients stayed cognitively normal (non-converters).

signalling.question: Are reasons for loss to follow-up and characteristics of those lost described?
signalling.quote: Six additional patients were excluded from data analysis because of excessive head motion during scanning (n = 1), MRI artifacts (n = 3), or poor MRI co-registration (n = 2).

domains.rationale: CBF was measured the same way for everyone, on one scanner with a vendor toolbox that has no user-modifiable parameters. However, co-registration was adjusted by hand and the paper does not say whether this was blinded to converter status. The factor (CBF change from V0 to V1) is measured over the same window in which conversion is determined, so it does not come before the outcome in time.

signalling.question: Is a clear definition of the prognostic factor provided?
signalling.quote: Regional CBF was calculated according to the parcellation of T1 images.

signalling.question: Is the method of measurement valid, reliable and the same for all participants?
signalling.quote: There were no user-modiﬁable parameters for generating CBF maps in the toolbox for ASL images.

signalling.question: Was the measurement free of unblinded subjective adjustment?
signalling.quote: Co-registration results were visually inspected and manually adjusted to ensure quality. (Searched for 'blind', 'masked' and 'unaware': no statement on blinding to converter status.)

signalling.question: Was the prognostic factor measured before the outcome occurred?
signalling.quote: Third, we explored whether converters showed a more signiﬁcant prefrontal CBF reduction than non-converters using repeated-measures ANOVAs (p < 0.05) with two factors, subgroups (converters and non-converters) and visit (V0 and V1).

domains.rationale: The baseline normal-cognition criterion refers to the Litvan level 2 PD-MCI criteria, and the battery covers five domains with two tests each. However, the paper does not state the criteria used to classify conversion at V1 or the normative source. It also does not say whether outcome assessors were blind to the imaging data.

signalling.question: Is a clear definition of the outcome provided?
signalling.quote: cognitively normal at V0, not meeting the diagnostic criteria of PDD (Emre et al., 2007) or level 2 criteria of PD–MCI

signalling.question: Is the method of outcome measurement valid, reliable and the same for all?
signalling.quote: Neuropsychological tests measured executive functions (Stroop Color and Word Test, Trail Making Test-B)

signalling.question: Was the outcome assessed without knowledge of the prognostic factor?
signalling.quote: Searched for 'blind', 'masked', 'unaware' and for the criteria applied at V1: none reported.

domains.rationale: Converters had 3.3 fewer years of education (FDR-significant). The converter comparison is a two-factor repeated-measures ANOVA with no covariates. Vascular risk factors and dopaminergic medication are not reported. The claim of independence from atrophy rests on separate unadjusted checks, not on adjustment.

signalling.question: Are important potential confounders measured?
signalling.quote: we asked whether the completion time of TMT-B or accuracy of Stroop Test at V0 or V1 correlated with prefrontal CBF, when prefrontal volume, UPDRS motor scores, depression scores, age, and education were controlled. (Searched for 'hypertension', 'vascular', 'diabetes', 'levodopa' and 'medication': none reported.)

signalling.question: Are the compared groups similar on important confounders?
Are important confounders accounted for in the design or analysis of the cited result?
signalling.quote: Converters were similar to non-converters at V1 in the total intracranial volume (p = 0.452), total cortical grey matter volume (p = 0.737), and the volume of prefrontal ROIs (ps > 0.150).

domains.rationale: The converter interaction was tested in 14 ROIs at uncorrected p < 0.05, while the other analyses were FDR-corrected. The single positive ROI (p = 0.036) is described as marginal. The reported statistics do not agree with each other: df of 96 with 49 participants, and partial eta squared of 0.90 for F = 4.66. The converter group has only 10 patients, and the authors acknowledge a likely bias and a risk of type 1 error.

signalling.question: Is the analysis appropriate, with multiplicity addressed?
signalling.quote: First, we examined whether patients with PD showed lower prefrontal CBF than HCs at V0 using two-sample t-tests or the Mann–Whitney U tests, if the data were not normally distributed (p < 0.05, FDR-corrected).

signalling.question: Is the presentation of the analysis adequate and internally consistent?
signalling.quote: A marginal subgroup diﬀerence was found in the left lateral orbitofrontal cortex, an interaction between subgroup and visit was found [F(1,96) = 4.66, p = 0.036, partial η2 = 0.90]

signalling.question: Is the sample size adequate for the analysis?
signalling.quote: First, the small patient pool subsequently led to fewer patients in the converter subgroup, thus, probably resulting in bias.

signalling.question: Is there no selective reporting of results?
signalling.quote: No eﬀect of the subgroup was found in any other prefrontal ROIs (ps > 0.145).

overall: High risk of bias (QUIPS: confounding and statistical analysis high; participation, prognostic factor measurement and outcome measurement moderate; attrition low).
overall_rationale: Two QUIPS domains are high risk. First, the converter comparison ignores a significant education imbalance and does not measure vascular or medication confounders. Second, the cited interaction is uncorrected across 14 ROIs, described as marginal, rests on 10 converters and is reported with inconsistent test statistics. Either of these alone makes the overall judgment high.

applicability.rationale: Early-stage PD patients (Hoehn and Yahr 1-2) from one Chinese movement disorders clinic; the finding concerns PD-MCI, not MCI in general.
